item.text:
**Bottom Line**
Mixed, leaning negative. I found some evidence of technocratic staffing and professionalized fiscal or education management, plus one small emergency-relief payment that was not obviously partisan. But I did not find strong 2024 evidence of a clean, depoliticized welfare system, and I did find clear evidence of political punishment through arrests, media repression, and opaque public-resource handling.

**Accepted Claims**
- [Soirée de solidarité nationale](https://www.primature.gouv.cd/2024/02/16/soiree-de-solidarite-nationale-representant-le-president-de-la-republique-le-premier-ministre-sama-lukonde-remet-un-cheque-de-15-milliards-de-francs-congolais-aux-victimes-des-affres-de-guerres-et/) | Primature | 2024-02-16 | The government, on Tshisekedi’s behalf, allocated 15 billion CDF for victims of war, floods, landslides, and internal displacement. This is real emergency relief, and it is not presented as a loyalty test, but it is small and does not show a broader anti-patronage welfare system. | IDs: 6B.7
- [DR Congo president names country's first female prime minister](https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/dr-congo-president-appoints-countrys-first-female-prime-minister-2024-04-01/) | Reuters | 2024-04-01 | Tshisekedi appointed Judith Suminwa, a planning minister and technocrat, as prime minister. That is weak but real evidence against purely patronage-based staffing around the top executive office. | IDs: 6B.7
- [Biographie de la Première Ministre](https://www.primature.gouv.cd/biographie-de-la-premiere-ministre/) | Primature | 2024 | Suminwa’s biography emphasizes applied economics, banking, UN/PNUD work, budget-ministry experience, and development-planning leadership. This supports a merit-based appointment reading rather than a pure loyalty distribution model. | IDs: 6B.7
- [ProfilMin.php](https://adminfinances.cd/ProfilMin.php) | Administration des Finances | 2024 | Doudou Fwamba is presented as a career finance official with economics and public-finance credentials and long ministry experience. That is evidence that at least part of the fiscal apparatus was staffed with professionals rather than obvious loyalists. | IDs: 6B.7
- [Deux nouveaux programmes avec le FMI](https://budget.gouv.cd/deux-nouveaux-programmes-avec-le-fmi-aime-boji-et-doudou-fwamba-etaient-devant-la-presse/) | Ministère du Budget | 2024-11-15 | The finance and budget ministers jointly presented the IMF programs and credited improved coordination since June 2024, with transparency in public-finance management highlighted as a reform goal. That is evidence of some professionalized fiscal coordination rather than pure patronage. | IDs: 6B.7
- [PEQIP school project](https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/press-release/2024/02/28/democratic-republic-of-congo-afe-expanding-and-equipping-primary-school-classrooms-for-better-learning-outcomes) | World Bank | 2024-02-28 | The education project explicitly used merit-based teacher recruitment, stronger information systems, and decentralized planning. This is the clearest evidence I found of a service-delivery program being designed around competence rather than political loyalty. | IDs: 6B.7
- [Congo election commission overspent, awarded opaque contracts](https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/congo-election-commission-overspent-awarded-opaque-contracts-report-2024-01-15/) | Reuters | 2024-01-15 | A civil-society report said CENI could not account for about $400 million and used opaque procurement. This is negative evidence for transparent public-resource handling and is compatible with capture or patronage networks. | IDs: 6B.7
- [DR Congo: activists’ arrests invoke déjà vu of growing repression](https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/02/dr-congos-arrest-of-activists-invokes-deja-vu-of-growing-repression/) | Amnesty International | 2024-02-16 | Security agents reportedly took LUCHA activists into unknown detention and used threats and violence. This is direct evidence of state punishment against dissent, even if it is not a classic welfare-benefits case. | IDs: 6B.7
- [DR Congo authorities must immediately free detained journalist](https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/03/drc-authorities-must-immediately-free-detained-journalist/) | Amnesty International | 2024-03-08 | Amnesty described Stanis Bujakera’s detention as judicial harassment meant to chill criticism. This is another direct example of political punishment through state power rather than neutral administration. | IDs: 6B.7
- [DRC president Felix Tshisekedi must be held accountable for human rights violations](https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/09/drc-president-felix-tshisekedi-must-be-held-accountable-for-human-rights-violations/) | Amnesty International | 2024-09-30 | Amnesty said the state of siege militarized daily life, concentrated power in military and police officials, and coincided with a crackdown on dissent. That is strong evidence of coercive political control, not a clean separation between welfare provision and punishment. | IDs: 6B.7

**Search Gap**
- I did not find a 2024 source directly documenting Tshisekedi personally using food, housing, permits, or jobs as explicit loyalty rewards or punishments.
- The evidence is mostly indirect: technocratic appointments and fiscal coordination on the positive side, and repression, opaque procurement, and state-of-siege coercion on the negative side.
